title: How many leaps before the cat catches the mouse?
description: A cat chases a mouse that starts forty eight feet ahead, and each leap of the cat is seven feet against five feet for the mouse. The board finds how much the cat gains in one leap, then how many such gains fill the head start. Keeko's doubt is that the two leaps should be added.
teaching_notes: One idea: both run the same way, so the cat closes the gap by the difference of the two leaps, and the head start is divided by that gain. Watch for children who add the two leap lengths.

video_script.why: The child can take away and divide, but has not yet seen a chase as a gap that shrinks by the same amount each leap.
video_script.substitution: The head start is the gap, and each leap shrinks the gap by the cat's leap less the mouse's leap.
video_script.anchor: a cat and a mouse on a straight line, the mouse forty eight feet ahead
video_script.wrong_move: adds the two leap lengths instead of taking the smaller from the larger
video_script.payoff_line: The cat catches the mouse in twenty four leaps
maths_rules: both run the same way, so in one leap the cat gains 7 - 5 = 2 feet
the gap of 48 feet closes by 2 feet each leap, so leaps = 48 / 2 = 24
check: the cat runs 24 x 7 = 168 feet; the mouse runs 48 + 24 x 5 = 48 + 120 = 168 feet; they are equal
video_script.design: One straight line, a cat and a mouse, the head start as a gap that shrinks. Assumes taking away and dividing. Keeko's doubt: add the two leaps.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about a chase.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A cat chases a mouse, and the mouse starts forty eight feet ahead.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The cat jumps seven feet every time the mouse jumps five feet.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>In how many leaps does the cat catch the mouse?

beats.on_screen: the chase stays on the board and Keeko sits beside it
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the cat leap bar with the mouse leap bar drawn inside it; the left-over part of the cat bar glows and is labelled gain

marks.m1: the cat leap bar and the mouse leap bar are drawn one over the other
marks.m2: the mouse bar sits inside the cat bar
marks.m3: the left-over part of the cat bar glows and is labelled gain

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The cat and the mouse run the same way.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The mouse's leap is already inside the cat's leap.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The extra distance the cat covers in one leap is called the gain.

beats.on_screen: Given: head start 48 ft; cat leap 7 ft; mouse leap 5 ft

marks.m1: the head start and the two leaps are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the mouse has a head start of forty eight feet. The cat leaps seven feet and the mouse leaps five feet.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of leaps in which the cat catches the mouse

marks.m1: the words number of leaps are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the number of leaps in which the cat catches the mouse.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: gain in one leap = cat leap - mouse leap = 7 - 5 = 2 ft

marks.m1: gain in one leap = cat leap - mouse leap is written
marks.m2: 7 - 5 = 2 ft is written and the gain glows

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, find the gain in one leap, because both run the same way. We take the mouse's leap away from the cat's leap.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seven minus five is two feet.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: number of leaps = head start / gain = 48 / 2

marks.m1: number of leaps = head start / gain is written
marks.m2: 48 / 2 is written with the gap cut into pieces of 2 ft

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, divide the head start by the gain, because every leap closes two feet of the gap.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Forty eight divided by two gives the number of leaps.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 24 leaps. Check: the cat runs 24 x 7 = 168 ft; the mouse runs 48 + 24 x 5 = 168 ft

marks.m1: 48 / 2 turns into 24 leaps and is boxed
marks.m2: the check lines for the cat and the mouse appear and both show 168 ft

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The cat catches the mouse in twenty four leaps.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Check, the cat runs one hundred and sixty eight feet. The mouse runs the head start and twenty four leaps, also one hundred and sixty eight feet.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the chase
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a doubt bubble shows 7 + 5 = 12 and 48 / 12 = 4; two arrows pointing the same way show the 5 ft leap inside the 7 ft leap; the bubble is struck through

marks.m2: two arrows pointing the same way show the 5 ft leap inside the 7 ft leap
marks.m3: the bubble is struck through and 7 - 5 = 2 glows

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks we add the leaps. Seven plus five is twelve, and forty eight divided by twelve gives four leaps.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But both run the same way, so the five feet are already inside the seven feet.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The leaps do not add. We take the five from the seven to find the gain.
